scope: Offline 3D reaction-vector-potential and conductor charge-continuity benchmarks. Uniform harmonic applied field, isolated nonmagnetic conductor. Not a moving PM motor or nonlinear ferrite/housing result.
implementation: ngsolve_eddy_av.py, NGSolve 6.2.2608, complex HCurl A plus conductor H1 potential, exact Coulomb multiplier or checked tree gauge, separate mean-zero conductor-potential multiplier. No penalty mass or fitted magnetic constants.

weak_disk.scope: Single pilot passes analytical weak-disk loss agreement and equation/current/power controls. Independent mesh, domain, quadrature and slotted-disk reference checks remain required.

electric_potential_order: Quadratic potential contains affine physical coordinates on the quadratic curved mesh. This brought isolated-volume current from 8.17e-9 in the original linear-potential pilot to 4.77e-17; current gate is 1e-9, unchanged from other closure controls.

sphere_reference.derivation: Match the interior l=1 spherical-Bessel potential to the vacuum field. Independently compute loss from dipole source work and interior electric-field volume integration; tests require agreement within 1e-9.
sphere_reference.purpose: Induced magnetic feedback is substantial, so this checks more than a weak-induction model.

tree_gauge.method: Remove higher gradient functions using HCurl(nograds=True), then fix a rooted spanning tree of lowest-order edges. Applicable only to the simply connected global field domain used here.
tree_gauge.verification: Small actual 3D FE tests compare tree and Coulomb gauges: current/loss, source work and reaction magnetic energy agree within 1e-8. Zero source and reversed harmonic-frequency controls also pass.
tree_gauge.scope: Equivalent gauge selection reduces algebraic cost. It changes no constitutive law, source or acceptance gate, and does not rescue the failed coarse sphere results.

gauge_check_followup: Higher-order tests exposed a 3.33e-8 reaction-energy difference from different automatic compound-space integration orders. Explicit identical tetrahedron rules remove that difference and retain the 1e-8 gauge-equivalence gate. Exact constraint scaling/iterative refinement improve algebraic conditioning without penalty terms or changed equations.

control_audit.unchanged_gates: 2% independent refinement; 5% analytical reference; equation/current/power controls

remaining: disk mesh/domain/quadrature controls and slotted-conductor independent comparison
coupled translating finite-PM transient and operating-speed controls
